levels.title: Beginner
levels.tagline: Start here if React is new to you
levels.description: Learn React from zero: what React is, how JSX works, how to build components, pass props, hold state, handle events, and render lists and forms.

tutorials.title: React Introduction
tutorials.description: What React is, the problem it solves, how it updates the screen, and how to write your very first component.

chapters.title: What Is React?
chapters.description: The problem React was built to solve and why so many teams reach for it.

chapters.title: How React Updates the Screen
chapters.description: Elements, the virtual DOM, and what actually happens when state changes.

chapters.title: Setting Up a React Project
chapters.description: The realistic ways to start a React project today, and what each one gives you.

chapters.title: Your First Component
chapters.description: Write, render and edit a real React component in the browser.

tutorials.title: JSX in React
tutorials.seoTitle: JSX Tutorial: Syntax, Expressions and Attributes
tutorials.description: How JSX works, how to put JavaScript values inside markup, how attributes differ from HTML, and how fragments let you return several elements.

chapters.title: What JSX Is
chapters.description: The syntax extension that lets you write markup inside JavaScript, and what it compiles to.

chapters.title: Embedding Values in JSX
chapters.description: Curly braces, which values render, and which quietly disappear.

chapters.title: Attributes and Styling
chapters.description: Why it is className not class, and how the style prop differs from a CSS string.

chapters.title: Fragments and Structure
chapters.description: Returning several elements, self-closing tags and the rules JSX enforces.

tutorials.title: Components and Props
tutorials.description: Split a UI into components, pass data down with props, use children for composition, and understand why props are read only.

chapters.title: Thinking in Components
chapters.description: How to break a screen into components and where to draw the lines.

chapters.title: Passing Props
chapters.description: How data flows from parent to child, and why props cannot be changed by the child.

chapters.title: Children and Composition
chapters.description: The children prop, and using components as slots instead of piling on options.

chapters.title: Props in Practice
chapters.description: Spreading props, forwarding the rest, and building a reusable component.

tutorials.title: State with useState
tutorials.seoTitle: React useState Tutorial: Managing Component State
tutorials.description: Add memory to a component with useState, understand why updates are asynchronous and batched, and learn the rules for updating objects and arrays.

chapters.title: Why State Exists
chapters.description: The difference between a value that survives a render and one that does not.

chapters.title: Updates Are Asynchronous
chapters.description: Why the value does not change immediately, and what batching means for your code.

chapters.title: Objects and Arrays in State
chapters.description: Why you must replace state instead of mutating it, and the patterns for doing so.

chapters.title: State in Practice
chapters.description: Sharing state between components and building a working counter.

tutorials.title: Events and Conditional Rendering
tutorials.seoTitle: React Events and Conditional Rendering Tutorial
tutorials.description: Handle clicks, keys and form submissions with React's synthetic events, then show and hide parts of the UI based on state.

chapters.title: Handling Events
chapters.description: Attaching handlers, the synthetic event object, and passing arguments.

chapters.title: Conditional Rendering
chapters.description: Ternaries, logical AND, early returns and when to use each.

chapters.title: Conditional Styling and Remounting
chapters.description: Toggling classes, and how keys decide whether React reuses or rebuilds an element.

chapters.title: Putting It Together
chapters.description: A short review of the pieces and how they combine into an interactive component.

tutorials.title: Lists, Keys and Forms
tutorials.seoTitle: React Lists, Keys and Forms Tutorial
tutorials.description: Render collections with map, choose keys that will not bite you, and build controlled forms with validation and submission.

chapters.title: Rendering Lists
chapters.description: Turning arrays of data into arrays of elements.

chapters.title: Choosing Keys
chapters.description: What keys are for and why the array index is usually the wrong choice.

chapters.title: Controlled Inputs
chapters.description: Binding form fields to state so React is the single source of truth.

chapters.title: Submitting and Validating
chapters.description: Handling submit, showing validation messages, and a full working example.

levels.title: Intermediate
levels.description: Go deeper into React with effects, refs, context, reducers, custom hooks and the composition patterns real applications are built from.

tutorials.title: Side Effects with useEffect
tutorials.seoTitle: React useEffect Tutorial: Effects, Dependencies and Cleanup
tutorials.description: Synchronise a component with the outside world: how effects run, what the dependency array really means, why cleanup matters, and when not to use an effect at all.

chapters.title: What an Effect Is
chapters.description: Synchronising with systems outside React, and when the effect body runs.

chapters.title: The Dependency Array
chapters.description: The three forms of the second argument and what each one means.

chapters.title: Cleanup
chapters.description: Returning a teardown function, and why React runs it more often than you expect.

chapters.title: When Not to Use an Effect
chapters.description: The four cases where an effect is the wrong tool, and what to do instead.

tutorials.title: Refs with useRef
tutorials.seoTitle: React useRef Tutorial: DOM Refs and Mutable Values
tutorials.description: Hold values that survive renders without causing them, reach into DOM nodes when you must, and forward refs through your own components.

chapters.title: What a Ref Is
chapters.description: A box React keeps for you, and how it differs from state.

chapters.title: Reaching into the DOM
chapters.description: Attaching a ref to an element, and the small number of jobs that justify it.

chapters.title: Forwarding Refs
chapters.description: Letting a parent reach the DOM node inside your component.

chapters.title: Refs in Practice
chapters.description: Two patterns worth keeping, and the mistakes to avoid.

tutorials.title: Context and Shared State
tutorials.seoTitle: React Context Tutorial: useContext and Prop Drilling
tutorials.description: Stop threading props through layers that do not need them. Create a context, provide a value, consume it with useContext, and avoid the performance traps.

chapters.title: The Prop Drilling Problem
chapters.description: What context is for, and the cheaper fixes worth trying first.

chapters.title: Creating and Using Context
chapters.description: The three pieces: create, provide, consume.

chapters.title: Context and Re-renders
chapters.description: The one performance trap everyone hits, and how to avoid it.

chapters.title: Context with a Reducer
chapters.description: The standard pattern for app-wide state without a library.

tutorials.title: useReducer and Complex State
tutorials.seoTitle: React useReducer Tutorial: Managing Complex State
tutorials.description: Move tangled state transitions into one reducer function, design clear actions, and know when a reducer beats several useState calls or a state library.

chapters.title: Why a Reducer
chapters.description: The point at which several useState calls stop being the simplest option.

chapters.title: Writing a Reducer
chapters.description: Purity, action design, and the signature in detail.

chapters.title: A Worked Example
chapters.description: A complete todo reducer, from actions to component.

chapters.title: Beyond a Reducer
chapters.description: When local state is no longer enough, and what the libraries actually give you.

tutorials.title: Custom Hooks
tutorials.seoTitle: React Custom Hooks Tutorial: Reusing Stateful Logic
tutorials.description: Extract stateful logic into functions you can reuse, learn the rules that make a function a hook, and build the handful of hooks every project ends up needing.

chapters.title: What Makes a Custom Hook
chapters.description: The naming rule, what gets shared and what does not.

chapters.title: Extracting a Hook
chapters.description: Refactoring a component into a hook, and choosing what to return.

chapters.title: Hooks Worth Writing
chapters.description: Four small hooks that show up in almost every project.

chapters.title: Lesser-Known Built-in Hooks
chapters.description: Three hooks that solve specific problems custom hooks often need.

tutorials.title: Component Patterns
tutorials.seoTitle: React Component Patterns: Composition, HOCs and Compound Components
tutorials.description: The patterns experienced React developers reach for: composition, compound components, render props, higher order components, and the APIs that support them.

chapters.title: Composition First
chapters.description: The pattern that removes the need for most of the others.

chapters.title: Compound Components
chapters.description: Components that work together and share state implicitly.

chapters.title: Render Props and Higher Order Components
chapters.description: The two pre-hooks reuse patterns, why they faded, and where they still fit.

chapters.title: Controlled and Uncontrolled Components
chapters.description: Designing a component that works both ways, the way the built-in inputs do.

levels.title: Advanced
levels.description: Master memoization, Suspense and transitions, error boundaries, portals, TypeScript with React, and testing components the way users use them.

tutorials.title: React Performance
tutorials.seoTitle: React Performance Tutorial: memo, useMemo and useCallback
tutorials.description: Find out what is actually slow before optimising, then use memo, useMemo, useCallback and list virtualisation deliberately rather than by reflex.

chapters.title: Measure Before Optimising
chapters.description: Why most memoisation is wasted, and how to find the real problem.

chapters.title: memo and Referential Equality
chapters.description: How React.memo works, and the reason it so often does nothing.

chapters.title: useMemo and useCallback
chapters.description: What each one caches, when it pays off, and what it costs.

chapters.title: Rendering Large Lists
chapters.description: The one optimisation that reliably matters, plus splitting work at the bundle level.

tutorials.title: Suspense and Transitions
tutorials.description: Declare loading states with Suspense, keep the interface responsive with transitions and deferred values, and lazy load components without jank.

chapters.title: Suspense Basics
chapters.description: Declaring a fallback once instead of threading isLoading everywhere.

chapters.title: Lazy Loading Components
chapters.description: Splitting the bundle with lazy and Suspense.

chapters.title: Transitions
chapters.description: Marking updates as non-urgent so typing never stutters.

chapters.title: Optimistic Updates
chapters.description: Showing the result before the server confirms it.

tutorials.title: Error Boundaries
tutorials.seoTitle: React Error Boundaries Tutorial: Catching Render Errors
tutorials.description: Stop one broken component taking down the whole app: write an error boundary, understand exactly what it can and cannot catch, and design sensible recovery.

chapters.title: Why Boundaries Exist
chapters.description: What happens without one, and the two lifecycle methods that make one.

chapters.title: What Boundaries Catch
chapters.description: The four categories they miss, and what to do about each.

chapters.title: Placing Boundaries
chapters.description: Granularity, recovery, and what the user actually sees.

chapters.title: Boundaries with Suspense
chapters.description: Combining loading and error states into one predictable shell.

tutorials.title: Portals and Rendering Control
tutorials.seoTitle: React Portals and Strict Mode Tutorial
tutorials.description: Render outside the DOM hierarchy with portals, build accessible modals, and understand what Strict Mode is really checking.

chapters.title: What a Portal Is
chapters.description: Rendering into a different DOM node while staying in the React tree.

chapters.title: Building an Accessible Modal
chapters.description: The parts a portal does not give you for free.

chapters.title: Strict Mode
chapters.description: What the double invocations are checking, and why not to switch it off.

chapters.title: Recap and Related APIs
chapters.description: A short tour of the remaining rendering escape hatches.

tutorials.title: React with TypeScript
tutorials.seoTitle: React TypeScript Tutorial: Typing Props, Hooks and Events
tutorials.description: Type props, children, events, hooks and refs the way experienced React teams do, and learn which patterns to avoid.

chapters.title: Typing Props
chapters.description: The base patterns for component props, including children.

chapters.title: Typing Hooks
chapters.description: Where inference is enough and where you need to help it.

chapters.title: Typing Events and Refs
chapters.description: Getting handler and DOM types right without fighting the compiler.

chapters.title: Generic Components and Practices
chapters.description: Components that adapt to their data, and the habits worth keeping.

tutorials.title: Testing React Components
tutorials.seoTitle: React Testing Library Tutorial: Testing Components
tutorials.description: Write tests that survive refactors: query the way users do, simulate real interaction, handle async updates, and know what is worth mocking.

chapters.title: What to Test
chapters.description: The guiding principle behind React Testing Library, and what not to bother with.

chapters.title: Queries
chapters.description: Finding elements the way a user would, in priority order.

chapters.title: Interactions and Async
chapters.description: Simulating real user behaviour and waiting for the result.

chapters.title: Mocking and Setup
chapters.description: Faking the network, testing hooks, and a checklist for good tests.

pageProps.description: Free React tutorials for beginner, intermediate and advanced developers. Short chapters, runnable code exercises and a quiz at the end of every tutorial.
